title: Rank Measures of Fine-Tuning Updates Need a Noise Baseline
abstract: arXiv:2610.22438v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Studies of what fine-tuning does to a language model often summarise the weight update $\Delta W$ by its rank. We compare the rank measures used for this against the same measures on a random matrix of the same shape, and against two harder references: the pretrained weights, and matched fine-tunes without alignment content. Measures that count directions put our fine-tuning updates only a little below noise; stable rank, computed from the same singular values, puts them far below. Both are right: an update has a few strong directions on top of a long tail. The pattern holds for thirteen released pairs up to 8B parameters, and it is not a mark of alignment: with training held fixed, instruction data does not stand out from Wikipedia or code, DPO gives the same update whether its preference labels are real or half swapped at random (one model, modest preference strength), and scrambled text gives the most concentrated update of all. translated_title: 微调更新的秩度量需要一个噪声基线
translated_abstract: 关于微调对语言模型有何影响的研究，通常用权重更新 $\Delta W$ 的秩来进行概括。我们将通常使用的秩度量与相同形状随机矩阵上的相同度量进行比较，并与两个更严格的参照对象进行比较：预训练权重以及不含对齐内容的匹配微调。计算方向数量的度量显示，微调更新仅略低于噪声水平；而由相同奇异值计算出的稳定秩则显示更新远低于噪声水平。两者都是正确的：更新是在一个长尾之上叠加了少数几个强方向。该模式在十三个参数量高达 8B 的已发布模型对上均成立，且这并非对齐的标志：在训练方式固定的情况下，指令数据与维基百科或代码数据并无显著区别；无论 DPO 的偏好标签是真实的还是被随机交换一半（单模型、中等偏好强度），其给出的更新都相同；而乱序文本反而产生最集中的更新。
tldr: 研究表明，微调权重更新的秩度量必须以随机噪声为基线来解读——更新实际呈“少数强方向叠加长尾”的结构，且这种秩结构并非对齐训练的独有特征。
en_tdlr: Rank measures of fine-tuning updates need a noise baseline: updates consist of a few strong directions atop a long tail, and this rank structure is not a signature of alignment.
